# Auto upgrade 0.9.0 to 0.10.0

Apply the mechanical parts of the Open Mercato `0.9.0 → 0.10.0` upgrade to a downstream app. Treat the matching section of `UPGRADE_NOTES.md` as the source of truth and leave every intent-sensitive change as an explicit manual finding.

The window is large: `0.10.0` is the first minor after `0.9.0`, so it also carries every fix that 0.9.x patch releases backported. An app already on a 0.9.x patch still runs every check — each is idempotent and a check that matches nothing is reported as a no-match.

## Scope

Operate on a standalone app or downstream repository that depends on `@open-mercato/*`. Never modify the framework monorepo, framework-owned `packages/`, dependency pins, lockfiles, generated output, vendored dependencies, or secrets. Run after the user has selected and installed `0.10.0`.

## Arguments

- `--path <dir>`: downstream repository root; defaults to the current directory.
- `--dry-run`: detect, classify, and report without editing files or running mutating commands.
- `--only <id[,id...]>`: limit work to named checks.
- `--skip <id[,id...]>`: omit named checks and record the omission in the report.

Reject unknown flags and combining `--only` with `--skip`.

## Upgrade checks

Rows follow the order of the `0.9.0 → 0.10.0` section of `UPGRADE_NOTES.md`.

| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `outbound-email-attachments-bytes` | Detect and report | Custom `ChannelAdapter` implementations whose capabilities set `fileSharing: true` and that read `attachment.url` in `convertOutbound`; imports of `assembleRfc2822` from `communication_channels/lib/email-mime`; callers writing `channelMetadata.outboundAttachments`; `send-as-user` callers passing `attachments`; tests asserting exact Gmail outbound message bytes | Report that the hub now fills `attachments` with bytes in `NormalizedAttachment.content` and an empty `url`. An adapter with `fileSharing: true` must send `attachment.content` (or use `resolveOutboundAttachmentBytes` from `communication_channels/lib/outbound-attachments`) and must not fetch `attachment.url`. Recommend the async `composeEmailMessage` over the deprecated `assembleRfc2822` (deprecated since 0.10.0, removal no earlier than 0.11.0). `channelMetadata.outboundAttachments` is now hub-owned and caller values are dropped. A malformed `send-as-user` `attachments` field now returns 422 with a stable `code`. Gmail tests may need the new header folding. Tests should assert on `content.attachmentDigests`. Adapters may declare `ChannelCapabilities.maxTotalBytes` (25 MB default) |
| `eval-case-tool-mocks` | No code action | N/A — additive enterprise eval feature | No action needed. Eval cases may declare `cases[].mocks`. An older CLI rejects eval-set files that use `mocks`, so upgrade every CLI that runs such files |

## Workflow

### 1. Gate the target

Resolve `--path`, require a regular `package.json`, and confirm at least one dependency or development dependency starts with `@open-mercato/`. Refuse to run when the target has the framework monorepo signature, including its core and shared workspace packages.

Inspect installed and pinned Open Mercato versions. Continue when they resolve to `0.10.0`; otherwise warn with the detected versions and require explicit user confirmation before edits. A dry run may continue without confirmation.

Exclude `.git/`, `node_modules/`, `.yarn/`, `.next/`, `dist/`, `build/`, `coverage/`, `.mercato/generated/`, generated registries, vendor directories, and framework-owned packages from every scan. Follow symlinks neither while scanning nor editing. Never print environment-variable values or other secret-bearing content: for every check that inspects an environment variable, report only its name, file, and line (and, for `OM_MCP_MUTATION_MODE`, only whether the value is outside `direct`/`deny`/`approval`).

### 2. Build and show the plan

Run every selected detection before editing. Report each match as `{checkId, file, line, classification, proposedAction}`. Distinguish exact automatic matches from detect-and-report candidates, and list every no-code-action reminder even when no file match applies.

For `module-runtime-requires`, the required modules are:

| Enabled module | Must also be enabled |
| --- | --- |
| `customers` | `progress`, `dictionaries`, `feature_toggles` |
| `portal` | `customer_accounts`, `feature_toggles` |
| `workflows` | `business_rules` |

An automatic match requires a regular `src/modules.ts` containing exactly one single-line object literal with `id: '<dependent>'` (or the double-quoted equivalent) and `from: '@open-mercato/core'`, and no entry anywhere in the file for the missing module id. A dependent entry spread across lines, built conditionally, pushed at runtime, or loaded from another file is a detect-and-report candidate. A dependency already present in any position is left where it is — order does not affect the generator check.

With `--dry-run`, print the complete plan, all no-code-action reminders, and unresolved manual work, then stop without edits, package-manager commands, generation, tests, or builds.

### 3. Apply bounded edits

Ask for confirmation of the displayed plan. Apply one minimal, idempotent edit per exact match:

- Insert `{ id: '<missing>', from: '@open-mercato/core' },` on its own line immediately before the exact dependent entry in `src/modules.ts`, once per missing module id, copying that line's indentation, quote style, and trailing-comma convention. When two dependents need the same module (`feature_toggles` for both `customers` and `portal`), insert it once, before the first of them.

Preserve file encoding, line endings, and unrelated formatting. Re-scan after editing: `src/modules.ts` must contain exactly one entry per required module id, while every manual candidate remains listed. Never perform repository-wide string replacement, and never run a database migration, a seed, an ACL sync, a reindex, or any other operator command without the user's explicit go-ahead.

### 4. Verify

Use the package manager and scripts declared by the downstream app; do not assume monorepo-only commands exist. Run, in order when present:

1. the configured generation script (this proves the `module-runtime-requires` dependencies are satisfied and surfaces duplicate module ids and non-literal `metadata.requires`);
2. the configured typecheck script (this surfaces the exact-decimal `*Exact` fields, the new `ToggleOutboundReactionResult` member, the `defaults.entryMode` setting key and other type-level changes);
3. the smallest affected test script, otherwise the configured test script;
4. the configured build script.

Stop at the first new failure caused by an automatic edit, revert only that edit, and move the match to manual follow-up. Preserve and report pre-existing failures rather than rewriting unrelated code or weakening checks.

### 5. Report

Report:

- the target path and detected Open Mercato versions;
- the complete pre-edit plan and user confirmation;
- every edited file grouped by automatic check ID;
- every detect-and-report finding, with exact file and line;
- every no-code-action reminder, no-match check, and skipped check;
- validation commands and outcomes;
- the operational follow-ups below that apply to the app, as an explicit checklist.

If no code changes were required, still report that all one hundred and six upgrade checks ran. Recommend reviewing the complete `0.9.0 → 0.10.0` section of `UPGRADE_NOTES.md` before deployment.

## Operational follow-ups

Report these as unresolved operator work; never run them on the user's behalf without explicit confirmation.

- Run `yarn mercato agent_orchestrator trace-retention:schedule` for organizations that existed before the retention worker shipped, and watch for the error code `agent_orchestrator.trace_content_retention_delete_failed`.
- Raise `OM_AGENT_RUN_TIMEOUT_MS` if `OM_OPENCODE_RUN_TIMEOUT_MS` was raised. After raising `maxSteps` in an `AGENT.md`, run `yarn generate`.
- Optionally delete plaintext blobs left by earlier versions from the `agent-trace-content`, `agent-trace-artifacts` and `agent-run-artifacts` namespaces.
- Restore price kinds that earlier seeds soft-deleted, using the note's SQL, before `seed-examples`. Then check `is_active` and clear the CRUD/API cache or restart.
- Stop workflow writers and workers, update all replicas together, then inventory, cancel and audit event-labelled workflow instances.
- Restart app and worker processes together for the EUDR undo fix; restart all workers for the communication channel concurrency fix.
- Provide a unique tenant encryption key of at least 32 bytes or Vault (`VAULT_ADDR`/`VAULT_TOKEN`) plus a dedicated `LOOKUP_HASH_PEPPER` where required. Use HTTPS for remote Vault, keep old keys and pepper, never regenerate keys for existing data, and follow `starters/docker/encryption-migration.md`.
- After upgrading all workers, purge entities from indexes their strategy pins exclude.
- Set the `OM_CSP_CONNECT_ORIGINS` / `OM_CSP_SCRIPT_ORIGINS` / `OM_CSP_STYLE_ORIGINS` / `OM_CSP_FRAME_ORIGINS` env vars at build and runtime.
- Pass `--allow-remote-database=host:port/database` for non-loopback PostgreSQL during setup.
- Set a unique `OM_INIT_SUPERADMIN_PASSWORD` before production init or reinstall, and rotate a superadmin credential that was set predictably.
- Apply the private next-interaction forward-only data migration, rebuild the customer entity/profile query indexes, and rebuild fulltext/vector indexes.
- Refresh `scripts/dev.mjs` and add `scripts/dev-encryption-preflight.mjs` in standalone apps. Keep the original encryption keys and Forms master key. Reserve exit status `78` in a custom `SYNC_ROLE_ACLS_COMMAND`.
- Review earlier customer comment attribution changes.
- Back up before rolling back the money migrations; their `down()` narrows precision.
- Use `TENANT_DATA_ENCRYPTION_OLD_KEY` for key rotation. `--deactivate-maps` requires an offline maintenance window and a restart of every replica.
- Apply the SSO migration before deploying the new code. Then enroll or rotate legacy SCIM tokens until the inventory query returns no rows.
- Align ingress limits with the 1 MiB signed-body cap, or set `OM_WEBHOOK_MAX_BODY_BYTES`.
- Reindex fulltext and vector data after the encrypted custom-field exclusion fix, and review copies held by external providers.
- Find integrations that use `/api/ai_assistant/tools/execute` for writes, migrate them, and review earlier direct mutations.
- Audit role ACLs and per-user ACLs for nested wildcard grants before upgrading, and replace unintended ones with explicit feature IDs.
- Set `MCP_HTTP_HOST` / `--host` or `MCP_DEV_HOST` for MCP servers reached from outside host loopback.
- Audit passkeys of uncertain provenance and re-enroll them through a trusted ceremony, keeping alternate MFA access.
- Customer search vectors: deploy to every app and worker, pause and drain vector jobs, purge `customers:customer_person_profile`, `customers:customer_company_profile` and `customer_accounts:customer_user` per scope, then `POST /api/search/embeddings/reindex` with `purgeFirst: true`. Also run `POST /api/search/reindex` if `purgeEntity` was used. Review external provider retention.
- Run the additive attachments migration (`attachment_partitions.access_resolver_requirements` plus backfill) before serving the new binaries, regenerate and build, and purge CDN copies.
- Invalidate cached public pay-link responses and review email templates for exposed content.
- Revoke and regenerate persistent MCP keys, then update client secrets.
- Apply `Migration20261027193000_receipt_scope` on PostgreSQL 15+ (needs a table lock) before resuming inbound traffic.
- Audit foreign-tenant or missing interaction author/owner references before replaying command history.
- Purge shared caches for `/api/attachments/file/*` and `/api/attachments/image/*`.
- Run the read-only ACL audit SQL before deployment, give tenantless super-admins an owning tenant, drain old instances, and invalidate the shared RBAC cache or wait out its TTL.
- Use Docker Compose 2.24.4+, recreate containers with the full file chain, move app-port health probes to the HTTPS hostname, and set `NEXT_PUBLIC_DOCUMENTS_COLLAB_URL` to a `wss://` URL.

## Rules

- Every automatic edit must be exact, bounded, minimal, and idempotent; the only automatic edit in this window is adding required module ids to `src/modules.ts`.
- Never change dependency versions, lockfiles, generated output, vendor files, framework-owned packages, or secrets.
- Never rewrite workflow definitions, agent definitions or `GOVERNANCE.json`, ACL grants, encryption configuration, CSP configuration, money arithmetic, search sources, attachment access resolvers, or adapter code automatically — every such match in this window is intent-sensitive.
- Never regenerate, rotate, or print an encryption key, pepper, superadmin password, API key, or any other secret; report only the variable name, file, and line.
- Never weaken typecheck, tests, or build to make the upgrade appear green.
- Always show the edit plan before mutation and the exact changed-file list afterward.
